_note: Retro-generated report for the historical 23.06 cycle that preceded the January 14, 2026 outage. Demonstrates what APEX would have surfaced if it had been running. Not used at the time; reference only.

header._historical_context: This is the cycle whose Conditional Pass classification was waved through under the temporarily-reduced 60% gate. Three months later, January 14, 2026 outage hit.

failure_analysis.summary: OpenShift operator subscription InstallPlanFailed for caas-orchestrator-operator.v2.0.4
Ansible playbook power_check.yml — idempotency violation on second run
CU-UP latency 6.1ms vs 5ms threshold (10/14 cores affected)
RT kernel cyclictest P99 32us vs 30us threshold (borderline)

deployment_recommendation.rationale: Pass rate 94.3% (below 95% target gate, above the temporarily-reduced 60% gate). Multiple P1 failures across CU-UP, OAM, and RT kernel suggest systemic load-handling pressure on Type-B nodes that should be investigated before wave deployment.
conditions_to_proceed: Vendor support engagement for RT kernel borderline
deployment_recommendation._retro_observation: If this cycle had run against a 95% gate (instead of the temporary 60%), the wave deployment would have been held. The temporarily-reduced gate is the most direct organizational cause of the January 14, 2026 outage. APEX surfaces gate-threshold changes in the Audit Lens — any future reduction now requires SRO + HQ Planning co-signature.
